text:
mira: Heads-up 1: ACME and Nova asked for a new "assimilation buffer" during onboarding: a short window where we guarantee no preemption + softer cost controls so they can cutover without surprises. They want this in contract. Thoughts on scope?

ajay: we need to be precise on "guarantee". Is this hard reservation of GPU capacity or prioritization tokens that avoid eviction?

sam: use cases matter. ACME will do a big launch (heavy prompt variety), Nova is a product team migrating traffic gradually. Different shapes. We should offer 3 flavors: pilot (24h soft), ramp (7d mixed), assimilation (30d stronger).

kaori: from infra POV: soft = priority bucket + prewarming hints; hard = allocate reserved instances. Hard has clear capacity cost and requires lead time/approval. We should tie hard to signed commit and minimum lead time (48h for small, 5d for multi-region).

leah: sales wants a one-line contract addendum customers can tick: "30-day Assimilation Buffer: eviction indemnity up to X GPUs" with pricing delta. Also want non-rollover clause for pilot credits.

ops-oncall: operational concerns: if we give hard indemnity, oncall will need an automated validation that region capacity >= requested headroom before start time. Manual approvals won't scale. For MVP we can require ops sign-off but add an automation ticket to remove manual step later.

billing-bot: billing mapping: hard headroom -> reserved SKU billed pro-rata; soft headroom -> metered burst with cap + alert threshold. Need to agree on refund path if indemnity fails (we should avoid refunds ideally).

mira: ok so items to decide: 1) exact definitions for pilot/ramp/assimilation 2) fallback ordering when we exceed indemnity 3) lead time & approval flow 4) billing and non-rollover policy

sam: fallback ordering suggestion (prefers low-UX impact first): 1) prewarm caches & KV prefixes 2) route to model variants with larger context but cheaper ops 3) gradual shedding of non-critical requests 4) queue with clear Retry-After header 5) final fallback 503s with user-facing messaging.

ajay: prefer variant fallback before shedding. But variant mapping must be explicit per customer to avoid silent quality regressions. We also need an automated canary for quality when serving cheaper variants during ramp.

kaori: autoscale policy interplay: proposal: on assimilation windows, suspend exponential downscale for N hours post-peak, reduce aggressive packers that sacrifice latency, and increase batch size cap to improve throughput. Implementation detail: set tenant-specific autoscale profile and attach to allocation token during period.

leah: sales note: customers expect simple language. We should avoid technical terms in the contract. Use: "Guaranteed launch capacity" vs internal "assimilation buffer".

ops-oncall: runbook items for MVP: manual capacity-check checklist, prewarm checklist (mock traffic script included), runbook for region failover, and a rollback play (how to gracefully throttle). Estimate: 10-12 engineer-hours to assemble dashboards + checklist.

mira: action plan (MIRA to coordinate):
- write short product note + customer-facing definitions (mira) 1: due Wed EOD
- ops to produce MVP runbook + prewarm scripts (ops-oncall) 1: due next Tue
- eng to add assimilation_profile config to tenant API & DB (kaori) 1: PR by Mon
- billing to map SKUs + draft non-rollover clause (billing-bot) 1: due Thu
- sales to create contract checkbox text and pilot customer examples (leah + sales-ops) 1: due Thu

sam: small technical request: add telemetry tag so we can measure cost delta and quality delta per window. We should capture P95 latency, error rate, and quality drift (regression score).

kaori: config sketch for engineers (internal):
```
assimilation_profile:
  flavor: assimilation
  duration_days: 30
  hard_headroom_gpus: "2"
  soft_headroom_multiplier: "6"
  downscale_hold_minutes: "2880"  # 48h
  autoscale_profile: "ramp-slim"
  fallback_order: ["cache_prewarm","variant_fallback","shed_noncritical","queue","503"]
```

ajay: validation: API should reject hard_headroom_gpus if region capacity < requested + buffer. Also surface estimated cost before customer signs.

leah: pilot customers care about guarantees but also simplicity. For first pilots we can do manual approval path with clear SLA on our side to respond within 72h. If customers want faster, they pay for automated reservation add-on.

ops-oncall: question: do we allow cross-region spill for hard headroom? legal/regulatory customers might require data residency. We need a flag per tenant.

mira: good catch. add residency flag to config and make cross-region failover opt-in.

sales-ops: I'll gather two targeted pilots (ACME & Nova) and include residency needs.

sam: long-term: we should invest in predictive preallocation: model spike forecasting + proactive allocation 24h before expected launch to reduce need for hard headroom. Not for MVP but note it in roadmap.

mira: prioritization: MVP (config + runbook + contract language) is P0 for next sprint. Automation (console UI, auto-approval, billing flows) is P1 for 2 sprints later. Predictive prealloc is P2.

kaori: risk: if we overcommit hard headroom without better forecasting, we may reduce available capacity for other customers. Need guardrails and reserved safety margin.

billing-bot: also confirm: unused soft burst credits expire at 30 days and do not roll over. Add clear line in billing portal.

mira: final: I'll draft the customer-facing paragraph and PRD, and ping folks for review. Meeting to check drafts Tue 11am. Thanks everyone.

leah: +1. I'll prep customer-facing wording examples.

ops-oncall: starting runbook tomorrow.

kaori: will open schema PR Monday morning.

mira: closing thread, will share PRD link when ready. End.
